title: Supported exterior products respect localization triangles
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $A$ a finite commutative ring, and $X,Y$ schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], separated in the diagonal sense [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Closed subschemes mean closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], and products are fibre products over $k$ [def-pc-base-change]. Write $p_X:X\times_kY\to X$ and $p_Y:X\times_kY\to Y$ for the projections. Let $B,C\subseteq X$ and $D\subseteq Y$ be closed subschemes, set $U=X\setminus C$, and let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with $F=p_X^*K\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*L$ bounded below. Use sections with support as in [def-pur-support-cohomology], derived tensor as in [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the supported exterior products of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product]. The three supported exterior-product maps
$$
\begin{aligned}
R\Gamma_{B\cap C}(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_D(Y,L)&\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{(B\cap C)\times_kD}(X\times_kY,F),\\
R\Gamma_B(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_D(Y,L)&\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{B\times_kD}(X\times_kY,F),\\
R\Gamma_{B\cap U}(U,K|_U)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_D(Y,L)&\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{(B\cap U)\times_kD}(U\times_kY,F|_{U\times_kY})
\end{aligned}
$$
form a morphism of distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category] in $D(A)$, the unbounded derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: the top row is the support-restriction triangle [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] for $(X,B,C,K)$ tensored with $R\Gamma_D(Y,L)$ and the bottom row is the support-restriction triangle for $(X\times_kY,B\times_kD,C\times_kY,F)$. In particular the square with the connecting morphisms commutes, using the shift identification of the exact tensor functor. The diagrams are natural under open restriction of either ambient scheme and under morphisms of $K,L$. Explicitly, for closed subschemes $D'\subseteq X$ and $B',C'\subseteq Y$, put $V=Y\setminus C'$. The three components
$$
\kappa^{D',B'\cap C'}_{K,L},\qquad
\kappa^{D',B'}_{K,L},\qquad
\kappa^{D',B'\cap V}_{K,L|_V}
$$
form a morphism from the support-restriction triangle for $(Y,B',C',L)$ tensored on the left with $R\Gamma_{D'}(X,K)$ to the support-restriction triangle for $(X\times_kY,D'\times_kB',X\times_kC',F)$. The third target term has ambient scheme $X\times_kV$. The boundary square uses the left-tensor shift identification $M\otimes_A^LN[1]\cong(M\otimes_A^LN)[1]$, represented on total tensor complexes by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{\deg(x)}x\otimes y$. The first-variable boundary uses $M[1]\otimes_A^LN\cong(M\otimes_A^LN)[1]$, represented by $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$. No assertion that any exterior-product map is invertible is made.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, the injective restriction sequence and its derived triangle; Tag 0F1E, remark-define-kunneth-map. Compatibility of the supported pairing and connecting morphisms is an agent-formulated refinement of these constructions.

proof.text: The fibre products and projections in the statement are the base changes supplied by [def-pc-base-change]. Pulling the closed immersions defining B, C, and D back along the projections gives the closed supports (B∩C)×ₖD, B×ₖD, and (B∩U)×ₖD; pulling back the open complement U gives U×ₖY. These identifications are immediate on affine charts from the fibre-product and closed-immersion definitions, and they also identify the analogous products D′×ₖB′, X×ₖC′ and X×ₖV in the second-variable formulation. More explicitly, on $\operatorname{Spec}R\times_k\operatorname{Spec}S$, the product of supports defined by $I\subset R$ and $J\subset S$ is defined by the sum of their extended ideals in $R\otimes_kS$. The intersection $B\cap C$ is defined by $I_B+I_C$, so both descriptions of its product with $D$ give the ideal generated by $I_B,I_C,I_D$. Taking the complement of the extended ideal of $C$ gives exactly $U\times_kY$.

Put N=RΓ_D(Y,L). By [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with R=A, the operation E↦E⊗ᴸ_A N is an everywhere-defined exact functor of derived categories, computed by K-flat models and canonical under changes of model. Apply this functor to the support-restriction triangle for (X,B,C,K) supplied by [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle]. The resulting distinguished triangle has exactly the three source objects displayed in the first row of the statement.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change); exact tensor functor on the one-point site

proof.text: Use coefficient sheaves to specify the resolution diagram. For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ put $S_Z=i_*A_Z$, with $A_Z$ the constant coefficient sheaf. For a bounded-below injective representative $I$ of $H$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], the complex $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_T(S_Z,I)$ computes $R\Gamma_Z(T,H)$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] for $A_T$ gives $0\to j_!A_{T\setminus Z}\to A_T\to S_Z\to0$. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}_T(-,I^n)$ is exact because $I^n$ is injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], its first kernel is exactly $\ker(I^n(T)\to I^n(T\setminus Z))=\Gamma_Z(T,I^n)$. These identifications commute with differentials. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] gives the asserted complex-level supported-Hom identification. Here and below global Hom complexes mean sections of the Hom complex of [def-pur-hom-complex]; a K-injective second argument is the derived Hom convention of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support); Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); supported-Hom model of the kernel of restriction

proof.text: For $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, set $E_0=S_{B\cap C}$, $E_1=S_B$, $E_2=j_!S_{B\cap U}$, where $S_Z=i_*A_Z$ for its closed immersion into its ambient scheme. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to $S_B$ and $(C,U)$. This identifies its open and closed terms with $E_2$ and $E_0$. Here is the check of the identifications: a closed immersion is finite [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] give stalk $A$ on the closed support and zero off it. Inverse-image stalks are [lem-weil-pbc-global-sections-stalk-comparison]. The restriction maps on nonzero constant stalks are the identity. The induced comparison maps are therefore isomorphisms by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]; for the open term use the presheaf construction [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and the counit specified by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Thus we have the specified short exact coefficient sequence $0\to E_2\to E_1\to E_0\to0$.

source.place: Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); Tag 04FX (lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion); coefficient support sequence and its external tensor product

proof.text: Every constant rank-one coefficient sheaf is flat, because tensoring with it is the identity. The closed-direct-image and open-extension clauses of [lem-sfb-open-closed-flatness], applied with the finite ring $A$ on the small etale sites, make $S_D,E_0,E_1,E_2$ flat. Their bounded complexes and cones are K-flat by [lem-kun-kflat-criteria]. On $P=X\times_kY$ its terms identify with $j_{P!}S_{(B\cap U)\times_kD}$, $S_{B\times_kD}$, and $S_{(B\cap C)\times_kD}$. To verify the maps as well as the objects, take the inverse of the coefficient comparison $\theta$ specified in [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] with both module inputs $A$; for the open term extend its restriction by the open counit. By [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] these comparisons on each geometric stalk are the multiplication $A\otimes_A A\to A$ when both support conditions hold and the map between zero modules otherwise. They are isomorphisms by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. The coefficient sequence arrows restrict constants identically where nonzero, so the same comparisons identify the arrows with the product coefficient sequence arrows. Taking $B=X$ in this coefficient comparison identifies $p_Y^{-1}S_D$ with $S_{X\times_kD}$, hence it too is flat by [lem-sfb-open-closed-flatness]. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], followed by tensoring with this flat sheaf, therefore preserves the short exact sequence of step 4.

source.place: Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); Tag 04FX (lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion); coefficient support sequence and its external tensor product

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-external-rhom-cone-pairing] with $a=p_X$, $b=p_Y$, the bounded flat coefficient complexes $E_i$ of steps 4–5, and $H=S_D$. Its hypotheses hold: $K,L$ are bounded below by assumption, $F$ is bounded below by the explicit hypothesis of the item, and all coefficient complexes and their cones are bounded flat. Writing $\mathsf H_T(E,H)=R\operatorname{Hom}_T(E,H)$, its specified maps are
$$\lambda_{E_i,S_D}:\mathsf H_X(E_i,K)\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_Y(S_D,L)\to\mathsf H_P(p_X^{-1}E_i\otimes_A^Lp_Y^{-1}S_D,F).$$
The cited lemma states that all three evaluation maps form a morphism of the contravariant coefficient-Hom triangles, with their connecting maps; it supplies the resolution-independent cone comparison rather than merely a completion of two squares. The degreewise convention is $(f\otimes g)(e\otimes d)=(-1)^{\deg(g)\deg(e)}f(e)\otimes g(d)$.

For $E_0,E_1$, step 3 identifies the Hom objects with supported sections, and step 5 identifies the product coefficient objects. These comparisons identify $\lambda_{E_i,S_D}$ with the specified supported exterior product [def-pur-supported-exterior-product]. Indeed $S_Z\otimes_A\underline M=C_i(M)$: multiplication of constant sections is an isomorphism on the stalks computed in step 4 and commutes with the quotient maps $e_i$. The Hom adjunction of step 3 is normalized by precomposition with $e_i$, exactly as in the cited definition. Thus its evaluation counit is the definition's $\epsilon_i$. Under these comparisons, the transpose defining $\lambda$ is the composite $\theta^L$ followed by the pulled-back $\epsilon_i\otimes\epsilon_d$ defining $\kappa$, since their precompositions with the coefficient quotient send $s\otimes t$ to $p_X^*s\otimes p_Y^*t$. Uniqueness of the quotient factorization and of the adjoint proves equality of these morphisms, and K-flat descent in the cited definition preserves that equality. For $E_2=j_!S_{B\cap U}$ the same identification is made on $U$ and then transported by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Its product ambient is $U\times_kY$, with precisely the comparison of [def-pur-supported-localization-comparisons]. This identifies the third specified map as well.

source.place: Tag 0F1E (remark-define-kunneth-map); comparison of the two evaluation normalizations

proof.text: Applying $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(-,I)$ to the coefficient sequence in steps 4–5 gives the degreewise short exact sequence $0\to\Gamma_{B\cap C}(X,I)\to\Gamma_B(X,I)\to\Gamma_{B\cap U}(U,I|_U)\to0$: step 3 identifies its first two complexes, and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] identifies the third. Restriction of $I$ to $U$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], with $j$ etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] identifies its third complex with the required derived sections. The product coefficient sequence gives exactly the corresponding product sequence by the same Hom-kernel identification of step 3, applied on $P$; its terms are those listed in step 5, with open ambient scheme $U\times_kY$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], these coefficient-Hom triangles have the actual connecting maps of [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle]. Step 6 gives a morphism between these triangles after exact derived tensoring, so it proves the boundary square for the specified three exterior products. No claim that tensoring an arbitrary injective section complex is exact is needed: on complexes of ordinary $A$-modules one may resolve the fixed tensor factor by a K-flat complex with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and the direct-sum total tensor then preserves the degreewise short exact sequence, because every summand is tensor with a flat module.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor); identify the coefficient-Hom sequence with the support-restriction sequence and its boundary

proof.text: On a total tensor complex the differential on a (p,q)-summand is d_E⊗1+(-1)^p1⊗d_F, by [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The canonical identification N[1]⊗ᴸ_A M≅(N⊗ᴸ_A M)[1] therefore sends x⊗y to x⊗y, whereas M⊗ᴸ_A N[1]≅(M⊗ᴸ_A N)[1] sends x⊗y to (-1)^{deg(x)}x⊗y. These are the shift identifications used in the boundary square; the displayed formulas follow by checking the two differentials on homogeneous tensors. This also shows that no sign is hidden in the first-variable formulation. Explicitly, for $x\in M^{p+1}$ regarded as degree $p$ in $M[1]$, the source differential on $x\otimes y$ is $-d_Mx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes d_Ny$, which is the differential of $(M\otimes N)[1]$. For $x\in M^p$ and $y\in N^{q+1}$ regarded as degree $q$ in $N[1]$, the source differential is $d_Mx\otimes y-(-1)^p x\otimes d_Ny$; multiplying by $(-1)^p$ in the target, and by $(-1)^{p+1}$ on the $d_Mx$ term, yields exactly the negative total differential in the shifted target.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), with its preceding construction and following sign-symmetry paragraph; direct computation with the total tensor differential and cochain shift

proof.text: For the second-variable clause put $V=Y\setminus C'$, $N=R\Gamma_{D'}(X,K)$ and $E'_0=S_{B'\cap C'}$, $E'_1=S_{B'}$, $E'_2=j_{V!}S_{B'\cap V}$ on $Y$. The sequence $0\to E'_2\to E'_1\to E'_0\to0$ is [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] for $S_{B'}$ and $(C',V)$; its stalk maps are the identity on $B'\cap C'$ and zero off that support, as verified in steps 4–5. Tensoring its pullback to $P$ with $p_X^*S_{D'}$ gives the product coefficient sequence with terms $j_{X\times V,!}S_{D'\times(B'\cap V)}$, $S_{D'\times B'}$, and $S_{D'\times(B'\cap C')}$. Apply the evaluation construction of steps 6–7 with the fixed first coefficient sheaf $S_{D'}$ and the varying second coefficient $E'$. Evaluation at constant sections gives respectively $\kappa^{D',B'\cap C'}_{K,L}$, $\kappa^{D',B'}_{K,L}$ and $\kappa^{D',B'\cap V}_{K,L|_V}$ [def-pur-supported-exterior-product]; the off-diagonal entry of a cone is now in the second tensor factor, so the total differential contributes $(-1)^{\deg(x)}$, exactly the second shift identification calculated in step 9. Applying Hom to the two coefficient sequences identifies the rows with [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] on $Y$ and on $P$ by step 8 and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. The left tensor functor is exact: the degreewise symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{\deg(x)\deg(y)}y\otimes x$ from [def-kun-derived-tensor] identifies it with the right tensor functor of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (the sign commutes with the total differential and carries K-flat quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms). This is the entire second-variable morphism, including its boundary square and its third ambient scheme $X\times_kV$.

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support), Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), Tag 0F1E (remark-define-kunneth-map); explicit second-variable coefficient sequence and evaluation

proof.text: For morphisms of K and L use the naturality of the defining adjunction counits and of the supported derived coefficient tensor comparison [def-pur-supported-exterior-product]. For open restriction, take the left mate of the actual supported restriction. Its counit equation identifies the evaluation on the cut factor with pullback of the original evaluation; for the uncut factor this is naturality of exact pullback-composition and projection comparisons [def-pur-supported-localization-comparisons]. Apply [lem-pur-supported-coefficient-open-tensor] for an open in X and [lem-pur-supported-coefficient-second-open-tensor] for an open in Y. Tensor naturality combines these coefficient squares with the two evaluation equations. The resulting equality is exactly the equality of the two adjoint transposes defining the supported exterior product, so injectivity of the supported coefficient adjunction proves both open identities. This is a genuine coefficient-level reduction, independent of the section inputs and their evaluation counits. The previously proved row restriction statement uses naturality of the normalized support triangle [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle], including its boundary comparison.

source.place: Tag 0F1E (remark-define-kunneth-map); coefficient and open-restriction naturality of the evaluation construction

proof.text: The source localization triangle is distinguished by mapping the normalized support triangle through the exact tensor-right functor; the target is distinguished by viewing the bounded-below external product as an object of the canonical plus subcategory and applying normalizedSupportTriangle_distinguished. The remaining component-extension conjunct is isolated as lem-pur-supported-product-localization-first-map.

The second-variable source is distinguished by tensor-left applied to the normalized support triangle, and the target by the same bounded-below plus-object argument. The remaining component-extension conjunct is isolated as lem-pur-supported-product-localization-second-map.

theorem supportedProductLocalizationFirst_map (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y B C D : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g] [IsSeparated g]
    (b : B ⟶ X) (c : C ⟶ X) (d : D ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion b] [IsClosedImmersion c] [IsClosedImmersion d]
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)))
    (L : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)))
    (_hF : ∃ n : ℤ,
      (externalProduct (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f g K.obj L.obj).IsGE n) :
    ∃ m : supportedFirstLocalizationSource A f g b c d K.obj L.obj ⟶
        supportedFirstLocalizationTarget A f g b c d K.obj L.obj,
      m.hom₁ = supportedFirstLocalizationComponent₁ A f g b c d K.obj L.obj ∧
        m.hom₂ = supportedFirstLocalizationComponent₂ A f g b c d K.obj L.obj ∧
        m.hom₃ = supportedFirstLocalizationComponent₃ A f g b c d K.obj L.obj
lean.note: The first-variable and second-variable conclusions and the two forms of naturality are the six theorem declarations in this module.
